worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{-{x}^{6}+4{x}^{2}-2}{{x}^{5}+8} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{-{x}^{6}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{4{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{8}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(-x+\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{5}})}{(1+\frac{8}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\text{ }\frac{-x+0-0}{1+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,-x \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
